answer_1.quote: We study the influence of LLM representations of gender in a downstream occupation prediction task. We demonstrate that gender representations in firstname embeddings can indicate biased behavior in LLMs for the high-stakes task of occupation prediction, despite some inconsistencies. To show that LLMs reinforce gender-occupation stereotypes, we conduct zero-shot prompting experiments to predict occupation from biographies.

answer_2.quote: Following De-Arteaga et al. (2019), we use true positive rate (TPR) to measure prediction gaps between female and male names. ... The bias coefficient, defined as the Pearson correlation of scatter points, reflects the strength of the linear relationship between the associated femininity of a name and the model's performance.
